questions.skillLabel: Nearest rotation to a drifted matrix
questions.prompt: A drifted orientation matrix is A = [[0.8, -0.6], [0.55, 0.75]]. The rotation R(phi) closest to A in the Frobenius norm has phi = atan2(a21 - a12, a11 + a22). Give phi in degrees (2 decimals).
questions.explanation: ||A - R(phi)||_F^2 = ||A||_F^2 + 2 - 2 tr(A^T R(phi)), and tr(A^T R(phi)) = (a11 + a22) cos(phi) + (a21 - a12) sin(phi), which is maximal at phi = atan2(a21 - a12, a11 + a22). Here a11 + a22 = 0.8 + 0.75 = 1.55 and a21 - a12 = 0.55 + 0.6 = 1.15, so phi = atan2(1.15, 1.55) = 0.63832 rad = 36.57°. (Normalising only the first column would give atan(0.55/0.8) = 34.51°, which is farther from A.)

questions.skillLabel: Axis of a rotation by pi
questions.prompt: R = [[-1,0,0],[0,0,-1],[0,-1,0]] is a rotation matrix with trace -1. Which axis-angle pair (unit axis, angle) gives exp([w]theta) = R?
options: w = (0, 1, 1)/sqrt(2), theta = pi, taking the positive square root of (r_ii + 1)/2 for each i
w = (1, 0, 0), theta = pi, since r11 = -1 marks the axis
w = (0, 1, -1)/sqrt(2) or its negative, theta = pi, since (R + I)/2 = w w^T
w = (0, 1, -1)/sqrt(2), theta = pi/2, since R is symmetric
questions.explanation: With theta = pi, exp([w]pi) = I + 2[w]^2 = 2 w w^T - I, so w w^T = (R + I)/2 = [[0,0,0],[0,.5,-.5],[0,-.5,.5]], which gives w = ±(0,1,-1)/sqrt(2). The positive square roots of the diagonal give (0,1,1)/sqrt(2), whose rotation by pi is [[-1,0,0],[0,0,1],[0,1,0]], with the wrong off-diagonal sign. The x axis rotated by pi gives diag(1,-1,-1), and an angle of pi/2 would give trace 1, not -1.
